items.detail: rkt_limits.py ran under C:/Python314/python (scikit-learn 1.8). The Block Q certifier pickle (pooler_all.pkl) fails to load under scikit-learn 1.9 in the maestro environment (ModuleNotFoundError: _loss). GCP code and tests ran in the maestro environment (Python 3.11). No model was refitted.

items.item: L1000 code written after the freeze
items.detail: PROTOCOL.md pre-specified the three L1000 analyses; rkt_limits.py was written after the freeze and is not hashed. The tier was already exposed, so these analyses are exploratory by declaration and select nothing.
For runtime the learning curve scores a fixed hash-ordered subset of 240 library compounds (387 active cells), not all 702. The subset is chosen by compound key only.

items.item: Post hoc diagnosis of zero map utility
items.detail: The finding that the sparse hub design puts 63 of 64 cells in one line, so admitted single-line rows cannot change other lines' fills, was diagnosed after rkt_memory.json showed exactly zero map utility. It is reported as a post hoc explanation and motivates experiment E4; it is not a confirmed hypothesis.

items.item: Post hoc descriptive analyses on fresh outcomes
items.detail: After fresh-evaluate, two descriptive summaries were computed from the saved choices and the exposed fresh outcomes: anchored decisions that differ from the no-anchor generic actions (112 of 141; 62 hits against 38 for the generic action), and hits per well-set with and without the anchor. Neither changes a pre-registered result; both motivate experiment E2.
The protocol states 12 downloaded plates. Preparation used 16 LVL3 plates (4 per line); the 4 A375 plates were already cached by the prior study, so 12 were new downloads.

maestro.endpoint_decision fits the logistic recalibration by Newton's method in NumPy; the frozen module used scipy BFGS. On the fresh references the parameters differ by at most 7.8e-08, every decision is identical and no abstention flips (verify.py).
